samples.question: The picture shows a plain background and an 8 by 8 square grid of 64 small marks, all painted in the same single dark colour on the same plain background. The 64 marks sit at equally spaced positions, with exactly the same spacing between neighbouring columns as between neighbouring rows, so no mark is closer to its left and right neighbours than to its neighbours above and below. Every mark is one of exactly two kinds and nothing else: a solid dot, whose middle is filled with the dark colour, or a hollow ring, whose middle is left empty in the background colour. Both kinds are drawn with the same amount of dark paint, so the two kinds cannot be told apart by how much ink they use, only by whether the middle is filled or empty. Score the picture as follows. For one horizontal row of 8 marks, its purity is the difference between the number of solid dots and the number of hollow rings in that row, taken as a positive number, divided by 8. The row score of the picture is the average of the purities of its 8 horizontal rows. The column score is defined in exactly the same way over the 8 vertical columns of 8 marks. One score is always strictly larger than the other; they are never equal. Nothing else matters: the background shade, the mark shade, the size of the marks, the spacing of the grid, the position of the grid on the canvas, the total amount of ink, how many solid dots and how many hollow rings the picture holds in total, and which kind sits in any particular corner all carry no information about the answer, and neither does any single row or column on its own, because only the average over all 8 rows and the average over all 8 columns decide it. Which score is larger, the row score or the column score? Answer rows or columns.
